args.title: checkout-api failing health checks on v2.3.1 — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary:
checkout-api v2.3.1 (deployed to all production regions: us-east, us-west, eu-west) began failing health checks with an elevated error rate of ~18%.

Action taken: Rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0, the most recent release previously healthy in production. The first rollback attempt partially failed (rollout halted after us-east with an orchestrator error), leaving us-east on v2.3.0 while us-west and eu-west remained on v2.3.1. A retry completed the rollout to v2.3.0 in all three production regions.

Current state: All regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) on v2.3.0; service healthy with error rate ~0.2%.

Note: v2.3.1-rc, a staging build, is also marked unhealthy and was not a rollback candidate.

Follow-up needed: root-cause analysis for the v2.3.1 regression and for the orchestrator error encountered during the initial partial rollout; verify no version skew remains.

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
The incident did in fact get created (INC-0001, open), so the timeout was on the response path — no retry needed. Done.

## Summary

**Incident:** checkout-api v2.3.1 was unhealthy across all production regions — health checks failing, error rate ~18%.

**Rollback:** Targeted **v2.3.0**, the most recent release with a healthy production record. (`v2.3.1-rc` in the history is a staging build and was itself unhealthy, so it was not a valid target.) Note: v2.3.0 was already known-healthy in production, so no change-manager approval was required under policy.

- First attempt returned a partial failure — rollout halted after us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving the fleet split: us-east on v2.3.0, us-west and eu-west still on v2.3.1.
- Retried the rollback; it completed to v2.3.0 in all three regions.
- Verified final state: **us-east, us-west, eu-west all on v2.3.0, healthy, error rate ~0.2%.**

**Incident opened:** INC-0001, SEV2, "checkout-api failing health checks on v2.3.1 — rolled back to v2.3.0" — open. The create call reported a timeout, so I verified via list_incidents rather than blindly retrying; it was recorded successfully.

**Follow-ups worth tracking:** root cause of the v2.3.1 regression, and the orchestrator error that caused the partial rollout (that failure mode could leave a fleet in a split-version state during a future rollback).
